skill.name: react-doctor
skill.description: Checks React projects after code changes for security, performance, correctness, and architecture issues using React Doctor.
skill.summary: Runs React Doctor after React changes to score quality and surface actionable diagnostics.
skill.author: millionco

security_audit.summary: The skill is prompt-only and contains no bundled executable code. It does instruct users or agents to run an external npx command, so the static external command finding is confirmed as a supply-chain execution risk.

remediation.issue: The usage command runs react-doctor@latest through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI version and ask users to approve the command before execution.

finding_verdicts.reason: The trigger is a Markdown code fence, but the fenced block instructs running npx -y react-doctor@latest. That downloads and executes an unpinned external npm package.

medium_findings.title: Ruby/shell backtick execution
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger is a Markdown code fence, but the fenced block instructs running npx -y react-doctor@latest. That downloads and executes an unpinned external npm package.

content.value_statement: React changes can hide security, performance, correctness, and architecture regressions. This skill runs React Doctor so teams get a score and prioritized diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the assistant to run the React Doctor CLI after React changes.
Reviews React codebases for security, performance, correctness, and architecture issues.
Uses verbose diff mode for change-focused diagnostics.
Reports a 0 to 100 score from React Doctor output.
Guides users to fix errors first and rerun the check.
limitations: Requires the external react-doctor CLI through npx.
Only targets React projects and React-related changes.
Results depend on the installed CLI package and project context.
Does not replace manual review, tests, or production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Check Feature Work
use_cases.description: Run diagnostics after finishing a React feature and identify fixes before review.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use score and diagnostics to focus review on risky React changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Releases
use_cases.description: Run a final React quality check and separate blocking issues from follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Check My React Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run React Doctor on this React project and summarize the score, critical issues, and first fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Feature Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current diff, then run React Doctor with verbose diff mode. Group findings by security, performance, correctness, and architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Fix and Verify Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use React Doctor results to plan fixes. Apply safe corrections, then rerun the check and compare the score.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Run React Doctor before release. Prioritize blocking issues, explain residual risks, and list follow-up work for nonblocking diagnostics.

output_examples.input: Run React Doctor after a component refactor.
output_examples.output: Quality score: 82 out of 100. Highest priority issue: effect dependency mismatch in the updated component. Next step: fix correctness first.

output_examples.input: Review the React diff before opening a pull request.
output: Performance: one memoization opportunity affects a changed list component.
Architecture: split shared state before expanding the feature.

best_practices: Run the check after meaningful React changes, not only at release time.
Fix correctness and security findings before performance or architecture cleanup.
Rerun React Doctor after fixes and compare the score with the previous result.
anti_patterns: Running the command without reviewing the package source or version policy.
Treating a high score as proof that the app is production ready.
Ignoring diagnostics because existing tests passed.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to run the React Doctor CLI with verbose diff mode.

faq.question: Does it include its own scanner code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a short prompt that calls an external CLI.

faq.question: What projects is it for?
faq.answer: It is intended for React projects and React-focused code changes.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a quality score and actionable diagnostics across security, performance, correctness, and architecture.

faq.question: Can it replace tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it with automated tests, manual review, and normal release checks.

faq.question: Why should I approve the command first?
faq.answer: The documented npx command executes an external npm package, so users should review it before running.
